## Himix 0.1

The first public Himix release. A derivative of [HypoMux v2.8.2](https://github.com/Hypostasis-Cat/HypoMux) (AGPL-3.0):
the engine is kept intact and the changes concentrate on the product layer.

### Downloads

| File | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Himix_Setup_0.1.exe` | Installer, recommended. Installs to `C:\Program Files\Himix`, registers the core service, creates shortcuts, uninstalls cleanly |
| `Himix_0.1_portable.zip` | Portable build. Unzip and run; writes no registry keys and registers no service. Full mode needs you to run it as administrator each time |

Both builds are functionally identical; they differ only in whether the core service stays resident.

### What this release changes

**Fully offline.** The upstream AI assistant, MCP bridge and background update polling are gone.
The app makes no outbound request at startup or while running; only when you press "Check for updates"
on the About page does it contact GitHub once.

**Rebuilt interface.** Navigation is a single labelled pill bar along the bottom. The mode choice moved
from "system proxy mode / virtual NIC mode" to "Light / Full", with each card stating what it does and what it costs.

**Less fiddly routing.**
- Rule input is auto-detected: pasting `https://www.example.com/item/123?id=5` adds `example.com`
- Outbound probing: after a rule is added, Himix probes which adapter can reach the target and rewrites
  the rule when the chosen line cannot
- In aggregation mode, if only one line can reach the target the rule is pinned to it, so intranet sites
  stop failing intermittently

**Automatic failover.** When an adapter disappears, rules pointing at it are projected onto the aggregation
pool, and the original routing is restored once the link returns or the app restarts.

**Packaging.** Both an NSIS installer and a portable zip. Setup is transactional: files and registry are
snapshotted first and any failed step rolls back, so a half-installed state cannot happen.

### What aggregation can and cannot do

It aggregates **many independent connections**; it does not split a single TCP connection across paths:

- Good for: IDM, Steam, Epic, EA App, Xbox, WeGame, large browser downloads — anything that opens many connections
- Not for: a single-connection transfer is still bound by its own link and will not get faster
- Lower latency is not the goal. Competitive games, voice and video calls are better served by direct rules
  or by pausing aggregation

### Requirements

Windows 10 / 11 (64-bit)

### Notes

- **The installer is not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher.
  Verify against the SHA-256 below
- Released under AGPL-3.0. Distributing it — including handing a build to a colleague — requires making
  the complete source available
- Use it only on devices and networks you own or are authorised to use
